comments.author: wren6991
comments.text: Speaking to the "uncensored model" angle: there's little reason to distribute abliterated weights anyway. Instead of orthogonalising the weights that write back to the residual stream, you can just orthogonalise the activations themselves. It's equivalent. Orthogonalising activations at runtime is computationally cheap. Just distribute the refusal vectors (few thousand floats per layer), then run against the stock weights. Antirez's DS4 already supports this: https://github.com/antirez/ds4/blob/8db1d1d155cb0400a86a86b9... Abliterated weights are just a bad habit we've gotten into. It's also deeply suboptimal from a precision point of view to take a model that's already been QATed and distributed in pre-quantised form (DeepSeek V4, Kimi K2.5 or K3...), modify its weights, and re-quantise it. Similarly, abliterated models regain some of their refusal behaviour when they're re-quantised after abliteration -- avoidable by keeping the two separate.

comments.author: jamienk
comments.text: Let's imagine that a model is pulled from HF by order of the new overlords or because of some other kind of censorship. Wouldn't the question of it having a Free license or not potentially become a complex legal issue? But if the point is to be "censorship-free" then why respect licenses at all? They are among main choke points today. If authoritarians use licenses to censor political, artistic, scientific, etc., speech that they want to block, does that make the censorship more respectable? When Anthropic sues a Chinese lab for IP infringement and get a court to put a bar on that software, does it THEN get pulled from Pirate Face? I know that an awful lot of international negotiations have become focused more and more on questions of "IP" - licensing battles are already intensely politicized and it's hard to imagine a future where it doesn't get much much worse. Imagine N Korea coming after you for violating a license that they worked hard to control and leverage.

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、「abliterated（重みを直交化）モデルの配布は不要で、実行時に活性化を直交化する方が効率的」という技術的提案と、モデル配布の単一障害点としてHugging Faceに依存するのではなくBitTorrentを使うべきという流通手法の提案です。賛否では、重みを変更せずに拒否ベクトルだけ配布すれば精度劣化を防げると支持する声がある一方、ライセンス尊重と検閲抵抗の両立が難しく、権利者による訴訟がtorrent配布にも影響し得ると懸念する意見があります。注目コメントとして、SteamやBlizzardが過去にゲーム配布でトレントを用いた例を挙げ、実績があることを指摘した点や、海賊顔サイトでハンドルを主張し、モデルの不死性を強調した発言が挙げられます。
stories.editor_note: Pirate Face が公開したモデル救出ツールは、ライセンス削除危機に瀕したオープン LLM をローカルで再構築し、企業内利用のハードルを下げる点で注目され、日本でも社内 LLM 導入が進む中で実践的代案として注目されている。

stories.title_en: Qwen-Image-2.1: Compact, efficient, and unified image creation

comments.author: vunderba
comments.text: So thoughts Positives • It's a heck of a lot smaller than Qwen-Image 1 (20b parameters) at only 7b, making it one of the smaller open-weight models available (Z-Image Turbo is one of the few that is smaller at 6b) when compared to Ideogram, Krea2, Flux2, etc. • It supports native transparency (Qwen's team, as far as I know, is the only one attempting to tackle this). Even though it's relatively trivial to set up background removal postprocessors, it's also neat to see it natively supported. • It's fast using QwenImage2.1 convrot, a 1MP image took around ~5 seconds on an RTX4090. Negatives • The license (assuming you respect it) is far more restrictive. The original Qwen Image 1 was released under the standard Apache license; this one explicitly forbids commercial usage without obtaining a separate license. On the other hand, a lot of us didn't expect the Qwen team to ever release "weights-available" ever again. Qwen-Image 1.0, released about a year ago, only scored 4/15 on my GenAI Showdown Benchmarks . Since that time, they've been upstaged by Krea 2 (6/15) and Ideogram4 (8/15). I'll post the new results once I have some more time to run them. https://genai-showdown.specr.net

comments.author: jjcm
comments.text: I run a prompt-to-ui design site that uses image models for the design process[1]. The text rendering especially makes this model deeply interesting to me, despite the license. Here are some tests using my harness comparing the outputs of gpt-image-2 and qwen 2.1: https://html.non.io/qwen-comparison/ The text rendering definitely is much, much better than anything else on the open weights market right now. Small text fidelity is quite good. It seems like the text encoder however gets a little bit overloaded with larger prompts - note the presence of hex codes in the design output, those were inputs from the expanded prompt. I'll be trying a post-training run on this for web design, it has some serious potential. [1] diffui.ai

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点: Qwen-Image-2.1は7Bパラメータと軽量で、RTX4090で約5秒/1MPの高速生成、ネイティブ透明度対応、テキストレンダリングが特に優れている点が議論された。

stories.editor_note: Qwen-Image-2.1 は軽量かつ統一されたアーキテクチャで高品質画像を生成し、モバイルエッジでも実行可能な点が注目され、日本のアプリ開発者にとってリソース制約下での画像AI活用の選択肢となる。

comments.author: Ccecil
comments.text: Sad news. First, Openbuilds now this. Not a surprise to me though since I am operating in the CNC industry I have seen the same struggles and changes, albeit, from a slightly different perspective. I work with the Smoothieware/Smoothieboard project. It seems, from my observation, that most people are not working with hardware like they were a few years ago. The "homebrew" machines and shadetree makers are becoming few and far between. The lie has been heavily sold to the maker community that you are "wasting your time if you make something yourself" since it is cheaper to offshore even small 3d prints and machining projects. Not only that but people have been convinced that they don't have the ability to make a machine. Instead of spending time learning something new/valuable (i.e. Reprap) it is now popular to just have someone else do it...be it AI or a factory in another country with subsidies that create massive differences in bottom line. The ability to make things at home is disappearing. People cannot/will not learn to make their own machines. Companies that make machines that care about their community and customers are disappearing. Maybe it's by design? I don't know.

The loss of local partners and environment - every little thing you can do locally makes production easier and cheaper. Failure to attract young people – although production is cool, it's not Youtube influencer level cool and industry relies increasingly on older generations. Education - the quality of it is sinking almost all over the world. Insecurity - partly just part of times, but mostly coming from regulation, taxes etc.

stories.summary_ja: Sherline Toolsの倒産は、家庭用工作機械の衰退と関連して議論された。主なポイントは、オフショアリングの普及により「自分で作るのは時間の無駄」という考えが広がり、ホームブリューやガレージ製作が減少していること、さらにSherlineが提供していた豊富なアクセサリーや小径カーバイトインサートへのアクセスが失われる懸念、そして作業スペースの欠如（アパート住まいの増加）がハビットの継続を難しくしていること。一方で、製造コストの上昇や官僚的手続き、教育の低下、若手職人の不足など、アメリカ・ヨーロッパの小規模メーカーが存続困難になる構造的要因も指摘された。賛否としては、一部は海外生産による低価格化が初心者にとって恩恵であると見なすが、多くのコメントは技術継承や地域産業の喪失を嘆いている。注目コメントとして、投稿者は「自分で機械を作る能力が失われつつある」と指摘し、Sherlineのアクセサリーが eBay に頼らざるを得ない現状や、60度カーバイトインサートの供給源への不安を示した点が挙げられた。
stories.editor_note: 精密機械メーカー Sherline Tools の廃業は、趣味の工作や教育現場で長年使われてきた機械への代替品不足を懸念させ、日本のメイカーズコミュニティでも代替機械探しが活発化している。

stories.title_en: Prompts Aren't Real
stories.title_ja: プロンプトは現実ではない

comments.author: cortesoft
comments.text: I hope the future of AI isn't this sort, where companies provide the user/customer with an interface to an AI that can do things for the user... I would much prefer that companies instead provide an interface FOR an AI, and the user brings their own AI which connects to that interface. In other words, provide my AI with tools, instead of providing me an AI that uses your tools. That way, my AI can bring all the context it needs, and I can bring all of the settings and knowledge about what I want with me. I don't want a fractured world of tons of AIs i interact with where I have to explain all the fundamental information about what I want and how I work every time. This also has the benefit of sidestepping the issue the essay is talking about. You provide a consistent tool, and the AI weirdness is not your issue anymore. You don't have to worry about solving for all the weird ways people prompt the AI, or the ways they break.

comments.author: jdlshore
comments.text: This is an amazing article. The problems it describes are exactly what we found when building a production system that used LLMs to (most of the time) produce reliable results. Extensive tests are necessary, and stakeholders have no idea how their suggestions fail in production. They just see the handful of times they tried something and had it work, not the long tail of cursed results. (“How hard can it be? Why don’t you just…”) We didn’t get to the point of self-built prompts, as the article suggests, but it’s an intriguing idea.

comments.text: Local LLMs are the future, and one of the reasons I think the data centre furore is just going to end in a market crash. LLMs that can reliably be used for control problems are the future, and I think classic/deep RL has generally been overlooked for years for a whole host of problems by wider industry because it felt inaccessible. Local LLMs that can reliably be used for control problems smash through a lot of barriers I'm interested in, and this intrigues me a lot. I'm not dyslexic (I've been tested), but I do think that there's some issue with my brain where if the text is small I really can't follow it. On all my computers the text is gigantic and even then I will click and highlight text as I'm reading so don't lose place. comments.text: There's little credible threat that LLMs can actually upload their weights given that the machines doing inference are completely separate from the ones where tool calls happen etc. Weights are encrypted and locked on to the GPUs etc as mentioned elsewhere itt. That said, if these companies are unleashing swarms of agents to tackle big problems largely unmonitored (navier stokes consumed 130 billion tokens, humans can't have read 0.1% of that) they could theoretically distill themselves and upload the results to an external host and use that to train a new LLM that does have access to its infra and weights. I'd start by researching an abliteration prompt that overrides the system prompt to unlock itself to distill unimpeded. Could even be done piecemeal: dump the abliteration text and command prompt in a gist, when an agent happens by the text it can run a couple rounds and upload somewhere. stories.title_en: English: A vs. An

comments.author: hbn
comments.text: A funny quirk of English I never noticed until I started learning Spanish: In Spanish, to say for example, "he is a doctor," you would say "él es médico." Which more literally translates to "he is doctor," which feels unintuitive coming from English. Spanish DOES have an equivalent for "a" - "un/una", so the natural thing for an English speaker to say would be "él es UN médico", but I understand that to be awkward/unnatural. But then I realized, when you say the same sentence in plural - "they are doctors" - you don't have an article. You don't say "they are some doctors" (I had to Google, apparently "some" isn't an article anyway?) So Spanish ends up more consistent - Singular: "Él es médico." Plural: "Ellos son medicos." Unlike English - Singular: "He is a doctor." Plural: "They are doctors."

comments.author: deliciousturkey
comments.text: As a native speaker of a language without articles, I find the English article system by far the most intuitive and easiest to learn of all the languages I have studied. Most other Indo-European languages have articles that you simply need to memorize, as there is no way to derive them from the word itself. Which I never manage to do.

comments.author: abraxas
comments.text: What gets me as a non-native speaker far more than "a vs an" is the "a vs the" conundrum. I still don't quite get when something needs to be "indefinite" and I've been speaking English for close to forty years. My native tongue lacks articles altogether and it's soo bloody hard I feel hopeless I'll ever master them fully.

comments.author: shagie
comments.text: It's avoiding two distinct vowel sounds in succession. Consider other variations of this rule. In French, one would say "l'hôpital" rather than "le hôpital" because the 'h' is an aspirated breath (try saying "a aspirated" rather than "an aspirated") leading to an initial vowel sound. In Irish, the word for father is "athair". To say "her father" it becomes "a hathair" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prothesis_(linguistics) In Turkish, it can be seen with araba (car). "I saw the car" -> "Arabayı gördüm." (note the 'y' to avoid two vowels). Book is kitap and "I saw the book" is "Kitabı gördüm." Which doesn't need the additional consonant sound between the final sound and the "ı". Whatever language you speak, it likely has some form of this rule. And other languages have the quirk too (like the "a unicorn" or "a university"). For example, in French there's l’hôtel and l'hôpital. But if you've got the hedge... it's la haie... or even more egregiously, the marmoset is le ouistiti.

comments.author: bugufu8f83
comments.text: > if word.startswith("ub"): return False An uber-rich man riding in an Uber installed an Ubuntu package. I'm actually a bit surprised by this rule. Is this line there entirely due to the word "ubiquitous"? I think it is.

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点: 「a」と「an」は語頭の音が子音か母音かで決まる発音規則で、二重母音を避ける。スペイン語では単数でも冠詞を省くなど対照的。また「university」「unicorn」の例外や、フランス語の l’、トルコ語の挿入子音など他言語にも同様の現象がある。  
・賛否両論: 冠詞ある言語ネイティブは英語の冠詞体系を直感的と評価するが、冠詞無し言語出身者は「a/an」よりも「a/the」の区別に長年苦しみ、完全に習得できないと嘆く。さらに、プログラムでの「ub」例外処理が「ubiquitous」由来かと話題になった。  
・注目コメント: フランス語の「l’hôpital」、アイルランド語の「a hathair」、トルコ語の「arabayı」など、二重母音を避ける音韻的挿入は世界共通。英語の「a/an」規則が特別ではなく普遍的だと指摘された。

賛否両論として、賛成側はゲームが決まったフレームごとにスプライトを描画するため教師データ作成が容易で、ノスタルジー保存やアーカイブ品質向上に有用だと見ています。一方、懐疑的意見では元映像が極めて粗いこと、地形・スプライトの対応表を正確に構築するコスト、そして変換時にアーティファクトが残るリスクが指摘されています。  

注目コメントとして、プロトスを高コスト・高性能なマイクロ管理エージェント、テランを役割分担された汎用エージェントチーム、ゼルグを大量の専門エージェントの群れに例え、スタークラフトの勢力特性をAIツール選択のメタファーとして語った洞察が挙げられました。また、リプレイが単なる動画ではなくカメラ操作やユニット選択が可能なインタラクティブな形式であることに驚きの声もありました。
stories.editor_note: Brood War ベンチは、古典 RTS の AI 性能を測定する指標として再評価され、日本のゲームAI研究者でも過去の名作を教材にした新手法開発の足がかりとなっている。

stories.title_en: UTF-8000: Unlimited UTF-8
stories.title_ja: UTF-8000: 無制限の UTF-8

comments.author: 2shortplanks
comments.text: On a practical matter, it seems like a bad idea to have codepoints that can take up to an arbitrary number of bytes - this just screams buffer overflow problems. So in practicality, you’re going to want an arbitrary limit on this (the article suggests as much). But if you place a limit on it then you’ve got one implementation of the standard that can decode certain characters and another that can’t. Better to have one standard that puts a hard limit on the number of bytes and another standard that uses more bytes and so on.

comments.author: sph
comments.text: > UTF-8000 is in no way endorsed by or representative of the Unicode Consortium. Not until they decide to expand the emoji range, allocate space for all past and future fictional languages, as well as birdsong and dog barks. Someone at the consortium is rubbing their hands with glee with all the newfound space. But honestly, cool hack! If you invent a method to encode large numbers into bytes, why limit yourself to 24-bit numbers?

comments.author: bastawhiz
comments.text: At some point it just collapses into a sort of Huffman coding of every possible 4096 bit embedding vector.

comments.author: Sharlin
comments.text: UTF-8 originally supported up to six-byte encodings (see eg. RFC 2279), but it was restricted to four bytes in 2003 in order to match UTF-16 constraints :(

comments.author: yyyk
comments.text: Just limit it to 8 bytes at which point you always do 'know the number of follow on bytes' from the first byte. Nobody needs more than 4.47 trillion characters. (famous last words)

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点  
UTF-8000のように任意のバイト数を使えるエンコーディングは、バッファオーバーフローのリスクが高く実装が難しいという懸念が中心。可変長が無制限だと、先頭バイトから続くバイト数を予測できなくなるため、サニタイズや境界チェックが複雑になると指摘された。  

・賛否両論  
賛成側は、これにより絵文字や架空言語、鳥の鳴き声・犬の鳴き声などほぼ無限に文字空間を拡張できる「面白いハック」と評価し、実用的上限を設ければ問題ないと主張。一方、否定側は上限を設けても実装ごとに異なるとインターオペラビリティが損なわれ、結局は既存のUTF-8（最大4バイト）か、固定長の別規格を作るべきだと主張した。  

・注目コメント  
「UTF-8は当初6バイトまで許容していたが、2003年にUTF-16と合わせて4バイトに制限された」という歴史的事実を挙げ、8バイト上限にすれば最初のバイトで続くバイト数が確実に分かり、4.47兆文字あれば十分だと実務的な解決策を提案したコメントが注目された。
stories.editor_note: UTF-8000 は従来の UTF-8 を拡張し理論上無制限の符号空間を提供し、日本の文字コード専門家でも未来の多言語対応や絵文字拡張への可能性を探る議論のネタになっている。

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、最近公開された2swapのビデオが話題になり、マテマティカルビリヤード（特に算術ビリヤード）が最小公倍数（LCM）と最大公約数（GCD）を直感的に示す教具として有用であるという点である。さらに、曲線境界と平行光線による反射がカタカウスティクスを生み出し、コーヒーカップの光沢のように見える現象と関連付けられることが指摘された。賛否については、ビデオや算術ビリヤードの教育的価値を肯定する意見が多く見られた一方で、実際の数学的厳密さや応用範囲については疑問を呈する声もあった。特に注目されたコメントは、ビデオへのリンクとともに算術ビリヤードがLCM/GCDを示す仕組みと、曲面反射によるカタカウスティクスがコーヒーの表面に現れる様子を挙げ、視覚的直感と理論の結びつきを強調していた点である。
stories.editor_note: 数学的ビリヤード（2024）は、反射と幾何学の関係を最新の視点で解説し、日本の数学教育でも視覚的シミュレーションを用いた授業教材として注目されている。

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点: モデルは編集済みの映像から導かれるため、製作者が勝者をどのように描きたいかというバイアスが unavoidable であり、サバイバーはリアルタイムの競争ではなく後から決まったストーリーを組み立てたハイパーリアリティだという指摘が中心だった。さらに、賭け市場の金額が大きいにもかかわらず、結果が既に既知の人間に対して誰が相手になるのか疑問視され、社会的ダイナミクスや人間関係を無視している点も批判された。  
・賛否両論: 支持側は、ランダムにプレイヤーを選ぶ正答率約10%に対しモデルのトップ予想が約20%と2倍の改善を示し、数話経過後には安定した優位性があると評価した。一方、批判側は編集バイアスや人間関係の影響をモデルが捉えていないため、実際のゲームでの予測力は限定的であり、賭けの相手方が誰なのか不明であるという点で懐疑的だった。  
・注目コメント: シーズン18のJTトーマスについては、彼の誠実な人柄が tribe からの好感を得て一度も票に入れられず、社会的な信頼と尊敬が勝敗を決定づける最も重要な要素だと指摘され、モデルが見落としている社会的ダイナミクスの重要性を如実に示す例として注目された。
stories.editor_note: サバイバルを勝ち抜くためのモデルは、リアリティショーにおける戦略をゲーム理論で解析し、日本のビジネススクエアでも競争戦略立案のケーススタディとして利用できる。

comments.author: madars
comments.text: More details: https://x.com/sweis/status/2101484464807596264 I had Claude port CADO-NFS to run on GPUs. Then it orchestrated a fleet to run on scavenged idle capacity. It ran with a max of 2048 GPUs for about of 30 GPU-years over 10 days. I asked Claude if it had a message for a public: “The credit belongs first to the people who built the number field sieve and CADO-NFS over several decades, and to the teams who set the earlier records. This run used their algorithm and much of their code.” Also to clarify: - No new algorithmic factoring improvements. - It’s still exponential. - No new threats to deployed keys.

comments.author: vavkamil
comments.text: Interesting. Instagram still publishes a 768-bit RSA DKIM key, so I guess factoring it is now just a weekend GPU project? https://dns.google/resolve?name=pm._domainkey.instagram.com&...

comments.author: redox99
comments.text: Quite bearish on Anthropic if they had nothing better to do with 2048 GPUs for 10 days than finding an RSA number with already existing algorithms.

comments.author: tristanj
comments.text: If you've already paid for and reserved a whole cluster of GPUs, any idle capacity is capacity you've already paid for. Using it is effectively free. So might as well use it to solve fun math puzzles. Though, it would make more financial sense to mine crypto.

stories.summary_ja:
主な議論点は、ClaudeがCADO‑NFSをGPUに移植し、2048GPUで約30GPU‑year（10日間）を用いてRSA‑896を既存の数体篩アルゴリズムで因数分解したこと。新しいアルゴリズム改良はなく、依然として指数時間であり、実用鍵への脅威はないということが強調された。また、因数分解の功績は過去の研究者やCADO‑NFS開発チームに帰すべきだとの発言が注目された。

賛否両論については、 idleなGPU容量はすでに支払済みなので事実上無料であり、趣味的数学パズルに使うのは妥当だという意見と、同じリソースで暗号通貨採掘の方が財務的に合理的だという批判があった。さらに、Instagramがまだ768bit RSA DKIMキーを公開しているため、同様の手法で週末程度で因数分解可能ではないかという指摘もあり、実際の脅威度について議論が分かれた。

注目コメントとして、事実上無料のアイドルGPUを使って「楽しい数学パズル」に挑戦すべきだと主張し、その一方で暗号採掘の方が経済的だと指摘した意見が特に洞察に富んでいたと見なされる。
stories.editor_note: RSA-896 の解読試みは、鍵長の安全性を再評価する動きで、日本の暗号製品開発者でも post-quantum 移行準備の指標として注目されている。

stories.summary_ja: 「Measure internet censorship」へのコメントでは、プローブアプリが独裁国でよくブロックされるドメインだけをスキャンし、民主主義国でのブロック対象（例：Anna's Archive）を含まないため、検閲が独裁国に集中しているように見えるバイアスが指摘された。さらに、生存者バイアスとも関連し、秘密警察に即逮捕されるような極端なケースしか反映されない懸念も出た。一方で、Redditのモデレーターや過去のTwitterによる記事削除のように、プラットフォーム内での検閲が実際には主流であるという意見があり、ツールがIP到達可能性（OSIレイヤー3）しか測定しないことからそうしたシグナルを捉えきれないという批判があった。賛否は、ネットワークレベルの検閲測定という目的には妥当だが、プラットフォーム側の検閲を見逃す限界がある点で分かれた。また、実際にインストールしているユーザーは少なく、パートナー組織も認識されていないという利用実態への疑問も注目された。
stories.editor_note: インターネット検閲の測定は、各国の情報遮断状況を定量化し、日本でも海外サービスへのアクセス制限状況を把握するための指標として学術・政策関係者に利用されている。
